seasonal_guidance.optimalWindow: July through early September, once SR 20 is open, the basin approach has melted out and the corner is dry

May.reason: SR 20 typically reopens across the pass in May, but the basin and the loose traverse toward Burgundy Col are still deep in snow.

June.reason: Snow lingers on the slope below Burgundy Col and on the traverse ledges, and the corner can seep after the spring melt.

July.reason: The approach to the 6,500 ft bench melts out and the corner, shaded until afternoon, is dry and pleasant on hot days.

August.reason: Driest, most reliable month; the morning shade keeps the jams cool, though late-summer wildfire smoke can settle over the pass.

September.reason: Still dry, but the corner stays shaded and cold until afternoon and shorter days squeeze a link-up with Burgundy Spire.

October.reason: SR 20 is usually still open, but the shaded corner is cold, early snow can coat the ledges, and the highway can close for winter any time.

June.reason: The south face can be dry, but snow still covers Andrews Pass, the lakes basin and the descent gully; an ice axe helps.

July.reason: Approach snow clears through the month; early on the upper chimney crux can stay damp. Mosquitoes and afternoon thunderstorms peak.

August.reason: Driest month with the approach snow gone; the low, shadeless miles of Andrews Creek are hot, and wildfire smoke or closures recur.

September.reason: Cool, dry rock in the chimney crux; the rifle hunt mid-to-late September brings hunters to the trails, and snow is possible late.

October.reason: First snow usually arrives this month; cold, short days on an 18-mile approach leave little margin, and larches peak early in the month.

evidence: Early-June party on Cathedral SE Buttress: rock dry, but much snow on approach and descent; axe useful - https://www.mountainproject.com/forum/topic/111910330/cathedral-peak-southeast-buttress-conditions

Pasayten backpacking: early July-early August snow typically cleared; mid-Sept colder nights, early snow possible; early Oct golden larches - https://www.skyestoury.com/blog/pasayten-wilderness-backpacking-guide
